additions.reason: The Torah's central bechina-category. Both seeking this-world reward and seeking next-world reward are explicitly declared to be aspects (בְּחִינוֹת) of belly-filling. This is the dominant node of Package 1 and must be added to the dataset.
additions.source_quote: וּשְׁנֵיהֶם הֵם בְּחִינַת מִלּוּי בֶּטֶן כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: The scriptural phrase referring to those who choose their portion in this-world life. The Torah explicitly identifies it as a bechina of מִלּוּי בֶּטֶן — these are those who fill their appetite with the vitality of this world.
additions.source_quote: חֶלְקָם בַּחַיִּים וּצְפוּנְךָ – הַיְנוּ הֵן אוֹתָן שֶׁבּוֹחֲרִין חֶלְקָם בַּחַיִּים, דְּהַיְנוּ לְמַלְאוֹת תַּאֲוָתָם בְּחַיִּים חִיּוּתָם בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

additions.reason: The scriptural phrase referring to God's hidden store, here applied to those who choose the world to come as their reward. The Torah makes this a bechina of belly-filling equal to the this-world seeker.
additions.source_quote: וְהֵן אוֹתָן שֶׁבּוֹחֲרִין בְּרֹב טוּב הַצָּפוּן, דְּהַיְנוּ עוֹלָם הַבָּא, וְזֶהוּ: וּצְפוּנְךָ... וּשְׁנֵיהֶם הֵם בְּחִינַת מִלּוּי בֶּטֶן כַּנַּ"ל

additions.reason: Defined as what remains after all appetites are satisfied — both money of desire and unholy children are called מוֹתָרוֹת. This is the dominant node binding the evil-surplus package.
additions.source_quote: הַמָּמוֹן שֶׁל תַּאֲוַת עוֹלָם הַזֶּה הוּא מוֹתָרוֹת, שֶׁנִּשְׁאָר מִן הָאָדָם מוֹתָרוֹת, אַחַר שֶׁמִּלֵּא תַּאֲוָתוֹ בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה

additions.reason: Unholy children are explicitly called מוֹתָרוֹת because they arise from the overflow/waste of the brain (שכבת זרע), making them the same essential thing as surplus money — both are the leavings of appetite.
additions.source_quote: גַּם הַבָּנִים שֶׁאֵינָם נוֹלָדִים בִּקְדֻשָּׁה, הֵם גַם־כֵּן מוֹתָרוֹת מַמָּשׁ, כִּי הֵם בָּאִים מִמּוֹתָרוֹת וְסִרְחוֹן וַעֲכִירַת הַמֹּחַ שֶׁיּוֹצֵא לַחוּץ

additions.reason: Cited from Avot 3 as the definition of unholy children — a rotten drop. The text calls this the bechina of those born outside holiness, establishing it as a face of the מוֹתָרוֹת domain.
additions.source_quote: מִזֶּה נִתְהַוּוּ הַבָּנִים, בְּחִינַת (אבות פ"ג) טִפָּה סְרוּחָה, סִרְחוֹן מַמָּשׁ

additions.reason: The word עוֹלְלִים is given the bechina definition of filth and impurity, via Rashi's commentary on Psalm 8. The text uses this as an aspect (בְּחִינַת) of the מוֹתָרוֹת/filth domain.
additions.source_quote: נִקְרָאִים הַבָּנִים עוֹלְלִים, לְשׁוֹן טִנוּף, כִּי עוֹלֵל פֵּרֵשׁ רַשִׁ"י (תהלים ח): טִנּוּף וְלִכְלוּךְ

additions.reason: Holy children are explicitly called a bechina of God's image/form. This is the positive counterpoint to Package 2 — where unholy children are filth, holy children complete and manifest God's image.
Holy children are described as very elevated and are explicitly paired with צֶלֶם דְּמוּת תַּבְנִיתוֹ. They are the positive bechina mirror of unholy children (Package 2).
additions.source_quote: וְגַם הַבָּנִים שֶׁהוּא חָפֵץ לְהַשְׁאִיר, כַּוָּנָתוֹ רַק בִּשְׁבִילוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ... כִּי הַבָּנִים דִּקְדֻשָּׁה הֵם גְּבוֹהִים מְאֹד

additions.reason: The verse ending 'אֶשְׂבְּעָה בְהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ' — 'Your image/form' — is identified as the holy dimension of the children's satisfaction. Waking/awakening God's image is the bechina of what holy children bring about.
additions.source_quote: הַשְּׂבִיעָה שֶׁל בָּנִים... הוּא רַק: בְּהָקִיץ תְּמוּנָתֶךָ, שֶׁעִקָּר שְׂבִיעָתוֹ שֶׁל בָּנִים הוּא רַק מַה שֶּׁהוּא מֵקִיץ וּמְעוֹרֵר בָּזֶה תְּמוּנָתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, בְּחִינַת צֶלֶם דְּמוּת תַּבְנִיתוֹ

additions.reason: David's ultimate choice — to behold God's face — is the supreme goal of service. This is the dominant node of the highest-level package. It is contrasted with the self-seeking of both other categories.
additions.source_quote: אֲנִי בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ... שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ... אָמַר, שֶׁבָּחַר לוֹ רַק לִזְכּוֹת בְּצִדְקוּת שֶׁלּוֹ לַחֲזוֹת פְּנֵי ה'

additions.reason: Knowing and recognizing the Creator is presented as identical in essence to beholding God's face — both are the supreme purpose of existence. The Torah states this is God's very will: that we recognize Him.
additions.source_quote: לִזְכּוֹת לְהַכִּיר אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ וְלָדַעַת אוֹתוֹ יִתְבָּרַךְ, שֶׁזֶּהוּ עִקָּר הַתַּכְלִית

additions.reason: Righteousness (צֶדֶק) is paired directly with beholding God's face: 'אֲנִי בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ' — it is through righteousness that one merits this vision. The Torah places צֶדֶק as an aspect of the same domain as חֲזוֹת פְּנֵי ה'.
additions.source_quote: אֲנִי בְּצֶדֶק אֶחֱזֶה פָנֶיךָ; שֶׁדָּוִד הַמֶּלֶךְ... בָּחַר לוֹ רַק לִזְכּוֹת בְּצִדְקוּת שֶׁלּוֹ לַחֲזוֹת פְּנֵי ה'

additions.reason: Natural death — dying when natural vitality (לַחוּת שָׁרְשִׁיִּית) runs out — is the bechina of the this-worldly person who lives out their full lifespan without interruption. The text identifies מִמְתִים מֵחֶלֶד as a category: those who are essentially children of this world.
additions.source_quote: מִמְתִים מֵחֶלֶד – הֵם בְּחִינַת בְּנֵי עוֹלָם הַזֶּה, שֶׁאֵין לָהֶם עוֹלָם הַבָּא, כִּי הֵם חַיִּים וְקַיָּמִים בָּעוֹלָם הַזֶּה בְּלִי שׁוּם עֹנֶשׁ, עַד שֶׁמֵּתִים מֵחֶלֶד

additions.reason: Root moisture is the physiological basis of natural lifespan — when it runs out, natural death follows. It is the bechina of the natural-temporal dimension of existence, and thus belongs with the natural-death cluster.
additions.source_quote: יֵשׁ שֶׁהֵם מֵתִים מִיתָה טִבְעִיִּית, שֶׁהֵם נוֹלָדִים בְּלַחוּת שָׁרְשִׁיִּית... עַד שֶׁנִּפְסָק וְנִכְלֶה לַחוּתָם וְחִיּוּתָם, וְהֵם מֵתִים מֵחֶלֶד

analysis_notes.good_evil_mirror_notes: Package 2 (מוֹתָרוֹת — unholy children, surplus money) is the evil mirror of Package 3 (צֶלֶם דְּמוּת תַּבְנִיתוֹ — holy children, God's image). Package 1 (מִלּוּי בֶּטֶן — self-seeking service) is the evil counterpart to Package 4 (חֲזוֹת פְּנֵי ה' — selfless service, beholding God). Package 5 (מִיתָה מֵחֶלֶד) is a neutral structural category describing the temporal nature of the this-worldly person.
